pages.title: 2026 Hyundai Tucson Spare Smart Key in Gainesville, GA
pages.summary: A genuine Hyundai smart key, matched to the car by its VIN and programmed in the owner's garage in Gainesville. No dealer appointment.
pages.result_short: Genuine Hyundai smart key programmed on site
pages.problem: The owners had just bought a used 2026 Hyundai Tucson Hybrid. The second key fob that came with it did not match the car, so they had only one working key.
did: Checked the exact key part number for this Tucson by its VIN.
Got a genuine Hyundai smart key with that part number.
Came to the car in Gainesville and programmed the new key in the garage.
Tested the buttons and the push-to-start with the new key.
pages.result: The Tucson now has two working smart keys, and the new one is a genuine Hyundai key.
pages.tip: Hyundai and Kia keys have to match the exact part number, not just the look. A fob that looks the same can still be the wrong one, so check it by the VIN before you buy.
pages.alt: New Hyundai smart key held in front of the Tucson steering wheel

pages.title: 2010 Toyota Corolla All Keys Lost in Cumming, GA
pages.summary: Every key to a 2010 Toyota Corolla was lost. A new flip key was cut and programmed at the car in Cumming, no tow and no dealer.
pages.result_short: New flip key cut and programmed at the car
pages.problem: The owner of a 2010 Toyota Corolla in Cumming had lost every key. With no key left there is nothing to copy, so the new key has to be made from the car itself: the blade cut to the locks and the chip added to the car's immobilizer.
did: Came to the car in Cumming, so it did not need a tow.
Made a new flip key from scratch and cut the blade for this Corolla.
Programmed the new key to the car and checked that it starts the Corolla.
pages.result: The Corolla has a working flip key again, made without any original key to copy.
pages.tip: If you are down to one key on a Toyota, a spare made from it costs less than an all-keys-lost job and takes less time.
pages.alt: New flip key for a 2010 Toyota Corolla next to the steering wheel

pages.title: 2015 Nissan Altima Smart Key Programming in Lawrenceville, GA
pages.summary: A 2015 Nissan Altima stopped accepting its smart key even though the fob was alive. A new smart key was programmed at the car in Lawrenceville.
pages.result_short: New smart key programmed, car starts
pages.problem: The owner's smart key for a 2015 Nissan Altima looked fine: the battery was good and the chip inside read normally. But the car would no longer register it, so the push-to-start did not work with that fob.
did: Came to the car in Lawrenceville and tested the owner's fob first: the chip was alive, the car simply refused it.
Programmed a new smart key to the Altima on site.
Checked push-to-start, lock and unlock with the new key.
pages.result: The Altima starts and locks with the new smart key.
pages.tip: The dash on this car also showed an "I-Key System Error". On this job that message came from a fault code (B2604) that points to the park/neutral position switch, not to the key. A new key does not clear it, so it is worth reading the codes before buying a fob.
pages.alt: New smart key for a 2015 Nissan Altima held in front of the steering wheel

pages.title: 2019 Ford Ranger All Keys Lost in Johns Creek, GA
pages.summary: No keys at all for a 2019 Ford Ranger. The door lock was decoded, two high-security flip keys were cut in the driveway in Johns Creek and both were programmed to the truck.
pages.result_short: Two new high-security keys cut and programmed
pages.problem: The owner of a 2019 Ford Ranger in Johns Creek had lost every key. The Ranger uses a laser-cut high-security blade (HU101), which cannot be copied by eye, and there was no key to copy anyway.
did: Decoded the driver door lock with a Lishi pick-decoder to get the key code.
Cut two new flip keys on the mobile cutting machine, right in the driveway.
Programmed both keys to the truck and checked the door, the ignition and the remote buttons.
pages.result: The Ranger went from zero keys to two working keys, with no tow and no dealer visit.
pages.tip: On high-security Ford keys every cut matters. If a new key turns the ignition but not the door, one cut was read between two depths; re-checking that position fixes it.
pages.alt: Two new flip keys for a 2019 Ford Ranger in front of the steering wheel

pages.title: 2021 Lexus RX Smart Key Programming in Cumming, GA
pages.summary: A new smart key for a Lexus RX in Cumming was programmed on site, and the remote buttons were synced so every button works.
pages.problem: The owner of a 2021 Lexus RX in Cumming had a new smart key that was not programmed to the car, so it could not start the SUV.
did: Came to the car in Cumming and programmed the smart key to the RX.
The lock and unlock buttons started working after the remote sync step was run a second time.
Tested push-to-start, the buttons and the doors before leaving.
pages.result: The RX starts on the key, and every button works.
pages.tip: If you buy a Lexus key online, check that it is the same part number as your original before paying. A key that only starts the car but has dead buttons usually needs the remote sync step, not a new key.
